result_kind: exact all-background one-site single-well theorem, quantitative minimum-curvature bound, and local-convexity obstruction
question: Can a nonconvex single-site or block functional-inequality theorem enter the BT Witten problem through uniformly controlled local fibers?
answer: Every one-site conditional BT action on an eight-regular lattice has exactly one critical point, its global minimum, despite possible negative curvature away from that minimum. The action curvature at the minimum is strictly greater than 13 before division by lambda^2. An exact 4^4 fixture has curvature -57 at another point, so local uniform convexity and direct convex Lu-Yau/Otto-Reznikoff imports are obstructed. The surviving local-to-global route is to prove a uniform one-site Poincare bound from this single-well structure and then control inter-site influence; neither step is claimed here.

one_site_reduction.fiber: z maps to psi+z*delta_o, with all other coordinates fixed
one_site_reduction.definitions: B_i=exp(psi_o-psi_i), A=sum_i B_i^-1, d_i=sum_(w~i,w!=o)exp(psi_w-psi_i)-q, C2=sum_i B_i^2, C1=sum_i B_i*d_i

single_well_theorem.quartic_minimum: the bracket has its minimum at x0^3=q*A/(2*C2), where it equals 3*A*(A-q*x0/2)
single_well_theorem.strict_sign: q<16 and A^2*C2>=q^3 imply x0<2*A/q, so every positive stationary value of P is strictly negative
single_well_theorem.conclusion: P(0)=-A^2<0, P(x) tends to +infinity, and every critical value is negative; hence P has exactly one positive zero. The fiber is coercive and that zero is its unique global minimum.

minimum_curvature.bound_chain: put y=A/x and K=A*sqrt(C2)>=q^(3/2); then F''>=2*K-q^2/2>=32*sqrt(2)-32>13 for q=8
minimum_curvature.coupled_action_bound: for S_lambda=A(lambda*phi)/lambda^2 in the log coordinate psi=lambda*phi, the corresponding one-site phi-fiber curvature at its minimum is also greater than 13
minimum_curvature.scope: curvature at the minimum only, not global strong convexity

nonconvex_fixture.field_modulo_constant: psi_0=0, psi_y=-log(2) at the eight neighbors of 0, and psi_z=-5*log(2) elsewhere
